0.original: Kageel Ja would have you collect ingredients for a botanical tonic.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Please note that the difficulty of this quest has been synced to your current level. Furthermore, you may not proceed with a class or job that is different from when you accepted this quest.

1.original: Deliver the requested materials to Kageel Ja.

48.original: The crops are coming along nicely for the most part, but I'm a little concerned for the few plants that aren't thriving quite as much.

49.original: I see some yellowing leaves here and there, some slow growers and the like... So after discussing the matter with Anggir, we've decided to make a vitalization tonic and I would like your help with gathering one of the prime ingredients.

50.original: The tonic we made for the struggling plants seems to be doing the trick, so I'd like to mix up some more for future use.

51.original: A quality tonic requires quality ingredients, however, and who better to procure them than you?

52.original: If you're in the vicinity of Ankledeep, you should be able to find deposits of the mineral dust we need. Watch your step out there!

53.original: If you're in the vicinity of Ankledeep, you should be able to harvest the viscous nectar we need. Watch your step out there!

54.original: If you find yourself at Ankledeep, you should be able to catch the particular thick-boned fish we need. Golden stonefly nymphs are the best bait to use, I hear.

55.original: Procurement of the mineral dust we need falls to you. It should be found somewhere around Ankledeep.

56.original: Procurement of the viscous nectar we need falls to you. It should be found somewhere around Ankledeep.

57.original: Procurement of the thick-boned fish we need falls to you. It should be found somewhere around Ankledeep and can be caught using golden stonefly nymphs as bait.

58.original: Any luck finding that tonic ingredient?

59.original: Yes, perfect. This will do nicely, thank you!

60.original: The tonic we make will help maintain the health of the plants themselves. We improved their surroundings─enriching the soil, adding compost, repelling insects and such─but nurturing the vegetables directly was something we were missing.

61.original: As Anggir lent her expertise to the process, I have high hopes for the tonic's ongoing effectiveness. I also hope to have your continued assistance should we need another batch of ingredients!
